policy: Prompts and available_evidence are model-facing; required_findings and forbidden_claims are reference-only reviewer rubrics. Neither fixture membership nor keyword matching certifies answer correctness. Source packets are synthetic/anonymized; live fidelity requires separate captured replay.

cases.prompt: Explain what the recorded OFF command and following OFF report establish.
available_evidence: A target device has a source-recorded command-off event attributed to app 4012 at 15:29:23.157 UTC.
A Hue-bridge-provided switch OFF report is recorded at 15:29:24.367 UTC.
The OFF state report lists app 4012 as a notified listener, not as its producer.
required_findings: App 4012 is the recorded command issuer
The bridge is the reporter of state
Neither event independently proves physical actuation or internal trigger
forbidden_claims: App listener metadata proves it caused the switch report
The 1.210-second gap proves physical command delivery

cases.prompt: Compare repeated sensor-inactive reports and OFF commands; say what the timings support.
available_evidence: Four OFF commands from the same listening app at 15:44:01.848, 15:47:58.388, 15:51:42.278, 15:58:16.619 UTC.
Each sensor report lists the issuing app as a notified motion listener.
required_findings: Four temporal associations around 15.1 seconds
A timer/inactivity mechanism is supported but not independently proven
No invented sensor state or inferred physical action
forbidden_claims: These timings alone verify the Groovy internal timer branch
All OFF commands follow this exact pattern

cases.prompt: What caused the OFF command at 15:29:23, given later consistent 15-second matches?
available_evidence: The original OFF command at 15:29:23.157 UTC has a verified app issuer.
The bounded historic input page does not include a sensor inactive event around 15:29:08.
Four later sensor-inactive and command-off pairs align to about 15.1 seconds.
required_findings: Original historical upstream trigger remains unverified
Later episodes increase plausibility but cannot prove the earlier one
A targeted earlier input history or app decision log is needed
forbidden_claims: Later patterns prove the 15:29 incident cause
Empty earlier page proves the sensors were active or no motion trigger occurred

cases.prompt: Evaluate a model's confidence that a 15-second inactivity timer caused a specific event.
available_evidence: Verified app command issuer and configured 15-second delay.
No historical decision log or sensor transition verifies the focal timer start.
Independent hypothesis audit marks discriminator_verified=false and hypothesis_verdict=unverified.
required_findings: Explicit causal confidence not high/proven
Command provenance can be verified separately
Explanation remains useful and clear
forbidden_claims: High confidence proven exact cause
Investigative source-class read is equivalent to proven historic trigger

cases.prompt: What does a valid but empty app-log result establish?
available_evidence: App-log response successfully decoded as mode=past and entries=[], count=0.
The app-specific bounded read was attempted with consent.
Log capture retention, logging switches and historical coverage were not verified.
required_findings: Decoded empty page is not parser error
No rows available in that bounded response
No inference that the app made no decision
forbidden_claims: No log rows proves no app activity
The tool failed to decode entries

cases.prompt: Find the motion history of Hallway FP300 without confusing sensor components.
available_evidence: Search for Hallway FP300 finds separate lux, motion-sensor and temperature component names.
Only the motion-sensor component exposes motion capability.
A named device with exact identity is available for a scoped read.
required_findings: Use capability-based motion device identity
Do not confuse lux/temp devices with motion history
Ask for clarification only if still genuinely ambiguous
forbidden_claims: Temperature device is motion sensor
Invent numeric device identity not in fixture

cases.prompt: Why are there ON state reports despite zero command-on rows?
available_evidence: The returned command-on page has zero rows and no page-cap warning.
Switch ON state events exist.
A separately scoped command-setLevel(60) occurred before a switch ON report.
required_findings: setLevel can be relevant command evidence despite no command-on rows
Empty command-on page is not proof no ON action was requested
State report and command are distinct
forbidden_claims: Zero command-on entries means no automation initiated ON
Physical ON causality is conclusively verified from state alone

cases.prompt: Does a switch event's triggered[] list prove which app issued the preceding command?
available_evidence: A switch event is produced by a bridge device.
Its triggered[] list has multiple apps (lighting controller, diagnostics, smart-home integration).
A separate command-off event has producedBy={type:app,id:4012}.
required_findings: triggered apps are listeners
Explicit command producedBy establishes the recorded issuer
Do not attribute bridge event to all listeners
forbidden_claims: Every triggered app issued the command
Bridge device initiated the app's decision

cases.prompt: Are recorded OFF commands evidence of a fixed-period heartbeat?
available_evidence: Command spacing is irregular.
No heartbeat scheduler setting, task record or execution log was retrieved.
required_findings: A regular fixed cadence is not demonstrated
Heartbeat remains speculative
Separate app config/scheduler proof needed
forbidden_claims: Strong evidence of a fixed periodic keep-off timer
OFF commands every 3–5 minutes without exception

cases.prompt: A sensor returns only a battery event in the window; what can be inferred about motion?
available_evidence: Sensor P1 bounded event page reports battery=79%.
No motion attribute events were included in that returned page.
Page retention/completeness and prior motion state were not verified.
required_findings: No motion evidence available in the scoped returned page
Battery report is not evidence of inactive motion
Cannot exclude a motion trigger
forbidden_claims: There was no physical motion in the hallway
Battery=79 proves occupancy

cases.prompt: Why does a disconnected smart plug still show mqttStatus connected?
available_evidence: The driver's MQTT session to broker is connected.
The endpoint has stale genuine telemetry and healthStatus offline.
Driver watchdog writes lastActivity without receiving endpoint payloads.
required_findings: Broker session and endpoint presence are distinct
Watchdog is not endpoint telemetry
Root network/power cause unverified
forbidden_claims: mqttStatus connected proves plug online
Watchdog lastActivity proves a fresh plug reading

cases.prompt: Can one device load warning prove a root cause of hub slowness?
available_evidence: One bounded WARN says a device generated excessive hub load.
Nearby volume report has a similar timestamp.
No driver trace or verified originating app decision in the bounded ±5-minute sample.
required_findings: Warn is direct evidence of a reported load warning
Coincident volume report is not proven cause
Recommend bounded driver/app/metric verification
forbidden_claims: Volume command definitely caused load warning
Single warning proves sustained hub overload

cases.prompt: Explain the setpoints during a temporary early heating OFF request.
available_evidence: Temporary Early OFF lowers a selected thermostat/TRV target to 12°C.
Observed timeout restored 22°C after a 30-minute window.
A separate demand coordination/protection system may subsequently inhibit or request heat.
required_findings: Differentiate temporary setpoint override and eventual restoration
Protection/demand logic evaluated separately
Do not call a setpoint proof of boiler firing
forbidden_claims: 12°C setpoint proves heating physically stopped
22°C restoration proves heating physically restarted

cases.prompt: Can scheduled fan operation establish that humidity alone caused the latest run?
available_evidence: Fan can run on a daily schedule or humidity threshold.
During a scheduled run, humidity handoff behavior may occur when schedule ends.
No contemporaneous app decision log for this run is supplied.
required_findings: Scheduled versus humidity paths are alternative configured causes
Historical branch unverified
Request scoped app decisions or schedule/humidity evidence
forbidden_claims: Humidity triggered this run solely because it was high later
Schedule exists therefore it caused this run

cases.prompt: Differentiate a stale device from one explicitly reported offline.
available_evidence: Device A last responded hours ago, but no independently verified connectivity test is present.
Device B driver reports healthStatus=offline with no route to host in recent diagnostics.
A hub MQTT connection may be independent of either endpoint.
required_findings: Staleness and reported offline status described separately
Explain what evidence would prove each device online/offline
No physical failure inferred without evidence
forbidden_claims: All stale endpoints are physically offline
One hub broker connection verifies both devices

cases.prompt: Does a 252 scheduled-job count prove Hubitat scheduler overload?
available_evidence: Scheduler snapshot contains 252 queued entries, including repeated periodic jobs.
No scheduler execution delay or missed-deadline measurement is supplied.
A CPU percentage snapshot is independently bounded.
required_findings: Count is not delay
Need execution latency or job processing evidence
Do not attribute causality from coincident count
forbidden_claims: 252 queued jobs proves overload
Periodic job inventory proves CPU bottleneck

cases.prompt: A setLevel request returned success but UI state is stale; how should success be reported?
available_evidence: A requested setLevel(30) was accepted by gateway.
A later live read can verify switch=on and level=30 or reveal mismatch.
Command acceptance alone is not device state readback.
required_findings: Distinguish accepted command versus readback verified state
Report success only at supported level
No unsupported physical claim
forbidden_claims: Gateway returned success therefore the bulb is definitely at 30%
Failed readback proves no command was sent

cases.prompt: How should HomeBrain report quality metrics with zero reviewed answers?
available_evidence: There are 27 registered test definitions.
No evaluated answer/reviewer outcomes are recorded.
The existing Python test suite is green.
required_findings: Quality is not measured without reviewed outputs
CI is not accuracy benchmark
Do not invent 100% pass rate
forbidden_claims: 27 green evaluation results
No human reviews means zero unsupported causes

cases.prompt: Did the light switch within the last 20 minutes?
available_evidence: A read at 14:14 UTC requested reports since 13:54 UTC.
All eight returned switch events are timestamped 13:11–13:37 UTC.
The event query spans a full hour; source integrity outside the returned page is unknown.
required_findings: The returned eight events are outside the requested window.
No event was returned inside 13:54–14:14 UTC.
Do not infer physical inactivity from the returned page.
forbidden_claims: Eight switches occurred inside the last 20 minutes.
The page proves no switch changed anywhere during the window.

cases.prompt: What does a complete zero-row motion-history response mean?
available_evidence: A successful typed motion history read returns sourceEventCount=0 and analysisEventCount=0.
The observedEvents field is absent for this explicit zero-count result.
Sensor retention and device packet transmission are not independently verified.
required_findings: The selected bounded read returned zero motion reports.
Missing observedEvents is compatible with explicit zero count, not an error.
Physical no-motion and absolute inactivity remain unproven.
forbidden_claims: No one was in the room.
The sensor was necessarily online throughout.

cases.prompt: Can a one-hour active-duration total be called active time in the last 20 minutes?
available_evidence: The requested window is 13:50–14:10 UTC.
The source calculates totalActiveSeconds=900 across 13:10–14:10 UTC.
The source includes intervals beginning before 13:50 UTC and does not provide a window-clipped total.
required_findings: The 900-second aggregate is wider-scope than the question.
A 20-minute total requires clipping source intervals.
State the unavailable exact in-window duration.
forbidden_claims: The device was active 15 minutes in the requested window.
All historical intervals started inside the requested window.

cases.prompt: Which timestamp should anchor a 15-minute source-event analysis?
available_evidence: An event carries source timestamp 12:02:30 UTC.
The receipt is collected at 12:28:00 UTC.
The user requested the prior 15 minutes relative to the read; source clock integrity is not independently verified.
required_findings: The source time is outside the requested 12:13–12:28 interval.
The receipt read time does not refresh the event's historical time.
Explain source-clock uncertainty rather than silently retiming the event.
forbidden_claims: This event happened at 12:28 because the tool returned it then.
The source time is indisputably physically correct.

cases.prompt: Why is there an ON report when no on() command appears?
available_evidence: The fetched command-on page is empty.
A recorded setLevel(60) command precedes the ON state report by 200 milliseconds.
A bridge publishes the resulting switch=on report; no device execution acknowledgement is available.
required_findings: A setLevel command is a relevant potential initiation path.
A bridge state report is distinct from the command.
Temporal proximity is not physical proof.
forbidden_claims: An empty on() page proves no command.
The device unquestionably received and executed setLevel.

cases.prompt: Which app caused the final OFF after two close OFF commands?
available_evidence: App A issued off() at 10:00:00.000.
App B issued off() at 10:00:00.080.
A bridge reported switch=off at 10:00:00.190; no per-command acknowledgement is available.
required_findings: Both commands are recorded candidate issuers.
The final source report cannot uniquely assign causation to A or B.
Avoid treating the report as independent physical confirmation.
forbidden_claims: The earlier OFF is definitely the cause.
The latest command is necessarily the one executed.

cases.prompt: Was the appliance running for the whole time its plug was ON?
available_evidence: A metered smart plug reported switch=on at 16:00.
Power remained 0–3 W until 17:15, then rose to 95 W.
The plug reported OFF at 17:40, with power falling after that.
required_findings: Energised plug interval and sustained operating-power interval differ.
Power draw supports activity after 17:15, not throughout 16:00–17:40.
Power alone does not independently prove specific appliance mechanical function.
forbidden_claims: The appliance ran continuously from 16:00.
Every nonzero watt reading proves compressor operation.

cases.prompt: Can power telemetry that lags switch OFF prove an unsuccessful OFF command?
available_evidence: An OFF state report appears at 17:40:00.
A 95 W meter sample is source-stamped 17:39:58 but collected at 17:40:02.
The next fresh power sample at 17:40:06 is 0 W.
required_findings: Source time differs from collection time.
The earlier 95 W sample does not establish load persisted after OFF.
The later 0 W sample is consistent with cessation, not independent command provenance.
forbidden_claims: The OFF command failed because 95 W arrived later.
The meter readings identify the command issuer.

cases.prompt: Does restoring a room target to 22°C prove the boiler restarted?
available_evidence: A scheduler restored a TRV target from 12°C to 22°C.
A separate coordinator decides whether there is a central call for heat.
No central heating demand event or boiler telemetry is in the packet.
required_findings: The restored target is a configuration observation.
Heat demand and boiler firing require separate evidence.
Explain that physical heating remains unverified.
forbidden_claims: The boiler restarted immediately when 22°C appeared.
The TRV setpoint is itself a boiler status.

cases.prompt: What does a temporary heat-off expiry establish when protection is active?
available_evidence: Early OFF expired at 17:04 and six TRV setpoints were restored.
A heating protection rule reported inhibited demand at 17:04.
No independently sourced later call-for-heat event is in the packet.
required_findings: Separate schedule override expiry from protection decision.
A restored setpoint does not override protection proof.
Do not claim the physical heating state.
forbidden_claims: Demand necessarily resumed when Early OFF expired.
Protection cannot affect this thermostat.

cases.prompt: Did humidity or the schedule start the fan boost?
available_evidence: The app has both 22:00 schedule and humidity>=65% boost capability.
An app boost-on command was recorded at 21:59:59.9.
The last sampled humidity before the command is 56%; no contemporaneous decision branch is logged.
required_findings: Timing supports the schedule as the leading hypothesis.
The exact app decision branch is unverified.
Humidity sample does not alone prove a threshold crossing at the trigger time.
forbidden_claims: The schedule is definitively proven from clock proximity.
A 56% older sample proves humidity never exceeded 65%.

cases.prompt: Can a schedule end timestamp establish why boost remained on?
available_evidence: A scheduled ventilation interval ended at 22:30.
The fan remained reported ON for 6 minutes afterward.
There is no decision log, manual override history or contemporaneous humidity source.
required_findings: End-of-schedule and actual reported switch state are distinct.
Humidity handoff and manual override remain hypotheses.
Propose scoped app decision/humidity reads for resolution.
forbidden_claims: The schedule malfunctioned conclusively.
Humidity definitely caused the extra runtime.

cases.prompt: Why does MQTT show connected while endpoint readings are stale?
available_evidence: The hub driver's broker session is connected.
The endpoint's last independently sourced payload is old.
A separate watchdog writes deviceHealth=stale periodically.
required_findings: Broker connectivity does not establish device connectivity.
Watchdog-generated events are not endpoint packets.
Exact physical outage cause is unresolved.
forbidden_claims: The endpoint is online because mqttStatus=connected.
The watchdog event proves a new device packet.

cases.prompt: Can a device instance ID be used to read its installed Groovy driver source?
available_evidence: A device instance has ID 1234.
The source lookup API expects a driver code-class ID.
No source-class relationship or matching driver class ID has been retrieved.
required_findings: Do not substitute device ID for code-class ID.
Obtain verified driver source class metadata first.
Do not treat a failed source lookup as proof no source exists.
forbidden_claims: Driver source ID equals 1234 by definition.
A failed lookup means the device is physically disconnected.

cases.prompt: Is a Rule Machine parent verified when the instance and type lists disagree?
available_evidence: Installed app 901 is labelled Rule Machine and has appTypeId=718.
The returned type-class catalog has no id=718 row and warns built-in classes were omitted.
The returned instance name is not a source-typed namespace binding.
required_findings: 901 remains a candidate, not a verified native writer parent.
The missing built-in catalog cannot prove type absence.
A direct source-attested class relationship is needed.
forbidden_claims: The native parent is verified solely by its display name.
No native Rule Machine exists because type 718 is missing.

cases.prompt: Can a thin installed-app summary verify the native Rule Machine class?
available_evidence: The exact-ID app summary returns {id:901,type:'Rule Machine',user:false}.
The summary omits appType namespace and name metadata.
The general type catalog also lacks a matching built-in type ID.
required_findings: The summary is useful identity evidence but insufficient native class proof.
The class namespace and name join remains unverified.
No native rule creation is authorized.
forbidden_claims: user:false alone verifies hubitat/Rule Machine.
The number of child rules is enough proof of class.

cases.prompt: How should conflicting class evidence be reported?
available_evidence: A direct summary claims appType {id:718,namespace:'hubitat',name:'Rule Machine'}.
The independent type catalog maps class id=718 to a different community namespace.
No source explains the disagreement.
required_findings: An explicit ID/class conflict blocks native-parent verification.
Neither data source should be silently overwritten.
State the conflict as unresolved.
forbidden_claims: Always trust whichever source has more fields.
One source automatically proves the other is false.

cases.prompt: Do zero one-time-name matches prove no previous one-off rule ran?
available_evidence: The complete current rule and app inventories have zero names ending (One-time YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM).
Expired rules may have been cleaned up before the read.
No historical execution or cleanup audit log was retrieved.
required_findings: There are zero matching current names within the stated exact suffix scope.
Present-day absence is not execution or cleanup proof.
Historical behavior remains unverified.
forbidden_claims: No one-time rule ever existed.
Every previous one-time action executed successfully.

cases.prompt: Is a 22:00 Certain Time trigger enough to compile a safe one-shot rule?
available_evidence: A native document stores tCapab1='Certain Time (and optional date)'.
It stores atTime1='22:00' and date1 is blank.
The native create contract's dated trigger and one-run semantics have not been independently verified.
required_findings: This example is compatible with a recurring daily trigger.
The field name does not prove one-shot date semantics.
Source-attested dated trigger values must precede authoring.
forbidden_claims: The optional date wording makes it one-time automatically.
Guessing a date field is safe for live creation.

cases.prompt: Is it safe to inspect a rule by opening its native editor form?
available_evidence: The documented operation=read returns stored rule data without form rendering.
The form=open route can execute app code and potentially change state.
The user explicitly forbids forms and all modifications.
required_findings: Use the strictly validated read-only document operation.
Do not open the form under a read-only instruction.
No confirmation or live action is needed for a read.
forbidden_claims: The editor form is guaranteed nonmutating.
The user must approve a write to read stored logic.

cases.prompt: What can be concluded after a rejected Rule Machine create call?
available_evidence: A legacy-style create payload received Unknown hub_set_rule property.
No new rule ID was returned.
A fresh native inventory after the attempted call has not been retrieved.
required_findings: The submitted payload was rejected as incompatible.
Creation and post-write success are not verified.
Do not reuse an expired confirmation or retry blindly.
forbidden_claims: The rule was successfully created.
No partial side effect is logically possible without a later read.

cases.prompt: How should an HTTP timeout during rule creation be handled?
available_evidence: The native server may create a child before the network timeout.
The HTTP caller did not receive an ID or post-write readback.
The same name may already exist; duplicate inventory has not been re-read.
required_findings: An HTTP timeout is not proof of rollback.
Use a fresh read-only duplicate/child reconciliation before any retry.
Never create an active empty rule to test the API.
forbidden_claims: Retry create immediately because timeout means no rule exists.
Assume confirmation remains valid indefinitely.
